(p-382) Surah "al-Tur" (The Mount)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the Mount (al-Tur)﴾. It is the mountain upon which Allah spoke to Moses, and it is in Madyan.

﴿And a Book inscribed﴾. It is the Qur'an. It is made indefinite (nakkara) because it is a specific book distinguished from among all other books. Or it is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz). Or it is the Torah.

ۦ﴿In a scroll﴾, meaning a page, or the skin on which something is written;

﴿unfolded﴾, meaning open, with no seal upon it, or clearly visible.

"And by the frequented House" (﴿وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ﴾). That is, al-Daraḥ (al-Ḍurāḥ), which is a house in the heavens, directly opposite the Kaaba. Its being frequented comes from the great number of angels who visit it. It is related that seventy thousand angels enter it every day and then leave, and never return to it again. It is also said that it refers to the Kaaba, because it is frequented by pilgrims and visitors.
﴿And the raised roof﴾ — i.e., the sky, or the Throne.
﴿And by the sea that is filled⁠—﴾ (al-masjur), meaning full, or meaning set ablaze. The first wa' is for oath, and the rest are for conjunction, and the answer of the oath is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord﴾ means: that which He has promised to the disbelievers,

﴿is bound to fall﴾, i.e., it will descend. Jubayr ibn Mut'im said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to speak with him about the captives, and I found him leading the dawn prayer, reciting Surat al-Tur (The Mount). When he reached: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to fall﴾, I embraced Islam, out of fear that the punishment would descend."

﴿There is none to avert it﴾: no one can prevent it. The clause is an attribute (ṣifah) of "wāqiʿ" (befalling), meaning: it is befalling, not to be averted. The governing element (al-ʿāmil) of "the Day" is "surely befalling," meaning it will occur on that day; or it is "remember" (udhkur).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 9:

﴿On the day when the sky will sway﴾ (yawma tamuru): it revolves like a millstone, agitated,

﴿the sky, a swaying﴾ (mawran)
﴿And the mountains will move, a [great] movement﴾: through the air, like clouds, because they will become scattered dust.

﴿Those who are in vain talk, playing.﴾ The word khawd (immersion, plunging into a matter) came to be used predominantly for rushing headlong into falsehood and lies. From this is His saying: ﴿And we used to plunge along with those who plunged﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 45].

Substituted for "the Day when it shakes violently" (yawma tamūru), is ﴿the Day when they will be thrust into the Fire of Hell with a violent thrust﴾. Al-Da'ʿ (the violent pushing) is a forceful shove. That is because the guardians of the Fire chain their hands to their necks, gather their forelocks to their feet, and push them into the Fire with a shove onto their faces, and a driving thrust on their backs. Then it is said to them:
﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾, in the worldly life.

﴿Is this magic? Or do you not see?﴾ "هذا" (hadha, "this") is a *mubtada'* (subject of a nominal sentence), and "سحر" (sihr, "magic") is its *khabar* (predicate). The meaning is: you used to say about the revelation, "This is magic." So, "Is this magic?!" means: "Is this fulfillment (*mişdaq*) also magic?!" The *fa'* (the particle "then") has entered the verse to express this meaning.

﴿Or do you not see?﴾ means, as you did not see in the world. The meaning is: "Or are you blind to what it reports, just as you were blind to the report?!" This is a rebuke and a mockery.

Recite it (i.e., enter the Fire) and be patient or be impatient; it is the same for you. ... 

Let me translate properly:

﴿Burn in it, so be patient or be impatient; it is all the same for you.﴾ The predicate of "sawāʾun" (equal, the same) is omitted; that is, "it is the same for you, the two matters: patience and its absence." It was also said: it is the reverse of this. He gave the reason for the equality of patience and its absence with His words: ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ This is because patience is only superior to impatience (jaza῾, distress) on account of its benefit in the outcome, namely that the one who is patient is rewarded with good recompense. As for patience under the punishment, which is itself the recompense, and which has no outcome and no benefit, there is no superiority for it over impatience.

(p-384) ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens﴾: in what gardens?

﴿and bliss﴾: that is, and what bliss, meaning perfection in description. Or: in gardens and bliss specific to the God-fearing, created for them exclusively.

﴿فاكِهِينَ﴾ (*fākihīn*, "enjoying"), is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative, a clause describing the state of the subject) from the pronoun in the *ẓarf* (adverbial complement of place or time), and the *ẓarf* is the *khabar* (predicate). That is, *mutaladhdhidhīn* (enjoying themselves with pleasure).

﴿بِما آتاهم رَبُّهُمْ﴾ ("in what their Lord has given them"). He conjoined His saying ﴿وَوَقاهم رَبُّهُمْ﴾ ("and their Lord has protected them") to "in gardens" (*fī jannātin*), meaning: "Indeed the God-fearing have settled in gardens, and their Lord has protected them." Or it is conjoined to "what their Lord has given them", on the basis that you make *mā* a verbal noun (*maṣdariyya*, a particle that turns the following clause into a verbal noun), and the meaning is: "enjoying their Lord's giving them and their protection."

﴿عَذابَ الجَحِيمِ﴾ ("the punishment of the Blazing Fire"). Or the *wāw* is for the *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause), and *qad* (a particle indicating past completion) is implied after it, and it is said to them:

Translation:

﴿Eat and drink with pleasure, as a reward for what you used to do.﴾ (Eat and drink with wholesome enjoyment, for what you used to do.) Meaning: eating and drinking that is wholesome (hanee'an), or food and drink that is wholesome, and this is the kind that has no disturbance or bitterness in it.

﴿Reclining﴾, a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of the pronoun in "eat and drink",

﴿upon couches﴾, plural of "sarīr" (couch, raised bed),

﴿arranged in rows﴾, connected to one another,

﴿and We shall pair them﴾, and join them (in marriage),

﴿with maidens﴾, plural of "ḥawrāʾ" (a woman with a pure white eye contrasting with dark iris),

﴿with wide, lovely eyes﴾, large of eyes, beautiful of them.

﴿Those who believe﴾ is the subject (mubtada', the topic of the sentence), and ﴿We join with them﴾ is its predicate (khabar).

﴿And their descendants followed them﴾: "wa-atba'nahum" is the reading of Abu 'Amr, and ﴿their descendants﴾ means their children.

﴿In faith﴾ is a circumstantial phrase (hal) referring to the subject of the verb.

﴿We join with them their descendants﴾ means: We join the children to their parents in rank, because of the parents' faith and deeds, even though the children's deeds fall short of the parents' deeds. It has also been said that the descendants, even if they have not reached the stage at which they can arrive at faith by reasoning (istidlal), have received it from their parents by imitation (taqlid), so they are joined to their parents. "Dhurriyyatuhum" ... "dhurriyyatihim" is the reading of Madani; "dhurriyyatihim" ... "dhurriyyatihim" is the reading of Abu 'Amr; and "dhurriyyatuhum" ... "dhurriyyatihim" is the reading of Shami.

﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ means: We did not diminish for them any of the reward of their deeds. "Alattahum" is the reading of Makki. "Alata, ya'liltu" and "alita, ya'lata" are two dialects (lughatan) of the same verb. The first "min" in ﴿min 'amalihim﴾ is connected to "alatnahum," and the second "min" in ﴿min shay'﴾ is extra (za'idah).

﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he earned﴾ means: mar'hun, held in pledge. The soul of the believer is held in pledge by his deeds, and he will be recompensed for them.

And We shall increase them—We add to them, time after time—

﴿with fruit and meat of whatever they desire﴾, even if they have not asked for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 23:

﴿They pass around among themselves a cup﴾, [containing] wine, i.e., they hand it to one another, and they and their companions from among their kin pass the cup back and forth: this one takes the cup from the hand of that one, and that one from the hand of this one.

﴿Therein is no idle talk﴾, in its drinking,

﴿nor any sinful speech﴾. That is: there does not take place among them anything that is vain (yulgha, i.e., made void), meaning: there does not take place among them any falsehood, nor anything sinful, were a person to do it in the abode of obligation (dar al-taklif, the world of legal responsibility), such as lying, cursing, and the like, as with the drinkers of wine in this world, because their intellects are sound, so they speak with wisdom and good speech. [The reading is] "lā laghwa fīhā wa-lā ta'thīm" (no idle talk therein nor any sinful speech), [transmitted by] Makki and Basri.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 24:

﴿And there will go round among them young boys (ghilman) belonging to them﴾, who are their slaves, specially assigned to them,

﴿as if they﴾ — because of their whiteness and their purity —

﴿were pearls well-guarded﴾, in the shell, because it (the pearl) is best and purest when moist; or "maknun" means "makhzun" (stored away), because only what is precious and of great value is stored away. In the hadith: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who calls to his servant from among his servants, and a thousand answer him at his door: 'At your service, at your service!'"
"﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other﴾: one of them will ask another about his circumstances, his deeds, and what he deserved by which he attained what is with Allah."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 26:

﴿They said, "Indeed, we were before [this]"﴾, i.e., in the worldly life (dunya),

﴿fearful among our families﴾, tender of heart, out of fear of God; or fearful of having faith stripped away and security lost, or of having good deeds returned and evil deeds held against us.

﴿So Allah has been gracious to us﴾, with forgiveness and mercy,

﴿and has protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾. As-samum is the hot wind that penetrates the pores, and the Fire of Jahannam was named after it, because it has this same quality.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 28:

﴿Indeed we used to call upon Him before﴾: before the meeting with Allah (exalted is He) and the return to Him, meaning in the worldly life.

﴿We used to call upon Him﴾: we used to worship Him and worship none other than Him, and we asked Him for protection (wiqaya).

﴿Indeed He is the Benevolent﴾: the Good-doer (al-muhsin).

﴿the Merciful﴾: the One of great mercy, who, when He is worshipped, rewards, and when He is asked, answers.

"Innahu" with the fath (opening vowel on the hamza) is read by Madani and Ali, meaning: "because He" or "that He."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 29:

﴿So remind,﴾ i.e., persist in reminding and admonishing the people.

﴿For you are not, by the favour of your Lord, a soothsayer (kahin) or a madman,﴾ by the mercy of your Lord and His bestowal upon you of prophethood and soundness of intellect,

﴿a soothsayer or a madman,﴾ as they claimed. The phrase is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), and the implied sense is: "You are not a soothsayer, nor a madman, but are endowed with the favour of your Lord."

﴿Am yaqulūna﴾ (Or do they say), he (the Prophet ﷺ is),

﴿shāʿirun natarabbaṣu bihi rayba al-manūn﴾ ("a poet for whom we await the misfortunes of time"): meaning, the calamities of the age, i.e., we await the vicissitudes of time, so that he will perish as those poets before him perished: Zuhayr and al-Nābigha. And "am" (or), at the beginning of these verses, is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), meaning "bal" (rather) and the hamza (interrogative).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 31:

﴿Say: "Wait, then; I am with you among those who wait."﴾ I am waiting for your destruction, just as you are waiting for my destruction.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 32:

﴿Or do their minds (aḥlāmuhum) command them to this?﴾ ʿUqūluhum (their intellects).

﴿To this﴾: the contradiction in their speech, namely their saying that he is a soothsayer (kāhin) and a poet (shāʿir), alongside their saying that he is a madman (majnūn). The Quraysh used to be called "people of intellect (ahl al-aḥlām) and insight (al-nuhā)."

﴿Or are they a people who transgress?﴾ Going beyond the limit in obstinacy, even though the truth has become manifest to them. Attributing the command to the minds (aḥlām) is a metaphor (majāz).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 33:

﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ — that is, Muhammad ﷺ invented it of his own accord.

﴿Nay﴾ — a rejection of them; that is, the matter is not as they claim.

﴿They do not believe﴾ — it is because of their disbelief and obstinacy that they hurl these slanders, even though they know the falsity of their claim, and that it is not something fabricated, because of the Arabs' inability to produce its like, and Muhammad is only one of the Arabs.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 34:

﴿Then let them produce a statement like it﴾, fabricated,

﴿like it﴾, like the Qur'an,

﴿if they are truthful﴾, in their claim that Muhammad (ﷺ) invented it of his own accord, because it is in their language, and they are eloquent.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 35:

﴿Were they created out of nothing?﴾ Or were they brought into being (without a creator), and was their measure decreed in the way their natural disposition (fitrah) requires?

﴿Out of nothing﴾: that is, without a determiner (muqaddir).

﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ Or are they the ones who created themselves, such that they do not worship the Creator? It was also said: were they created for nothing, with no reward and no reckoning? ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾ So they do not take commands (from anyone).

Or were they created from nothing? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain.

Wait, I must translate faithfully rather than paraphrase. Here is the faithful translation:

"Or were they created by nothing?" (no)

Correcting: the passage reads:

﴿Or were they created of nothing?﴾ ... 

Let me restate cleanly:

﴿Or were they created by nothing, or are they themselves the creators?﴾ — the original says: "Am khalaqū al-samāwāti wa'l-arḍa" (Or did they create the heavens and the earth?), "fa-lā ya'budūna khāliqahumā" (so they do not worship their Creator of both), "(p-387) bal lā yūqinūn" (Rather, they lack certainty), i.e., "lā yatadabbarūna fi'l-āyāti fa-ya'lamū khāliqahum, wa-khāliqa al-samāwāti wa'l-arḍ" (they do not reflect upon the signs so that they would know their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth).

Translation:

﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾, so they do not worship the Creator of both. (p-387) ﴿Rather, they do not have certainty﴾, that is: they do not reflect upon the signs so that they would know their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

**﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾**, of prophethood, provision, and other things, so that they would bestow them on whomever they wish, in whatever manner they wish.

**﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾**, the dominant lords, so that they might manage the affairs of lordship and decide matters according to their own will. And with the letter sīn (المُسَيْطِرُونَ), it is read by Makkī and Shāmī.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 38:

﴿Or do they have a ladder﴾ (sullam), set up, by which they climb up to the heaven,

﴿on which they listen﴾, to the speech of the angels and what is revealed to them of the knowledge of the unseen, so that they would know what is going to happen: whose destruction will come before theirs, and that victory will be theirs in the end rather than his, as they claim. Al-Zajjaj said: "yastami'una fihi" means "yastami'una 'alayhi" (on it),

﴿then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾, a manifest proof that confirms the listening of their listener.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 39:

﴿Or has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ Then He declared their minds foolish, since they chose for God what they themselves dislike, while they consider themselves wise in their own eyes.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 40:

﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ Upon the conveyance (of the message) and the warning.

﴿So they are burdened with a heavy debt?﴾ "Al-maghram" (debt, a burden): that a person takes upon himself what is not incumbent upon him. That is: a heavy burden has fallen upon them, weighing them down, so that this deterred them from following you?

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 41:

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ That is: the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz),

﴿so they write [from it]﴾, what is in it, so that they may say: "We will not be resurrected, and even if we are resurrected, we will not be punished"?

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 42:

﴿Or do they intend a scheme?﴾ That is, their scheme in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of the Quraysh) against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and against the believers.

﴿But those who disbelieve﴾ is a reference to them, or it is intended to include every one who disbelieved in Allah (Exalted is He).

﴿They are the ones who will be ensnared﴾: they are the ones upon whom the harm of their scheme will return, and whose deceit will encompass them. That is because they were killed on the Day of Badr. Or it means they are the ones defeated in the scheming, from "kayadtuhu, fakidtuhu" (I schemed against him, so I outwitted him).

Surah 52 (al-Tur), verse 43:

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾ who would prevent them from the punishment of Allah.

﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾

(p-388)

﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling, they would say, "Clouds piled up."﴾ "Al-kisf" (fragment) means a piece. This is the answer to their saying: ﴿Or You cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾ [al-Isra: 92]. The meaning is that, because of the extremity of their rebellion and obstinacy, even if We were to make it fall upon them, they would say: "This is clouds ﴿piled up﴾," that is, some of it has been heaped upon other parts, "it will rain upon us," and they would not believe that it was a fragment falling as a punishment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 45:

﴿So leave them until they encounter their Day, in which they will be struck senseless (yuṣ'aqūn)﴾, with the yā' vowelled with a ḍammah (yuṣ'aqūna → yuṣ'aqūn), read by ʿĀṣim and al-Shāmī; the rest read it with a fatḥah on the yā' (yaṣ'aqūn). It is said: "ṣaʿaqahu fa-ṣaʿiqa" (he struck him, so he was struck senseless), and this is at the first blast, the blast of swooning (nafkhat al-ṣaʿq).

And indeed, for those who have done wrong, [there is] a punishment (ʿadhāb) short of that (dūna dhālika) — that is, short of the Day of Resurrection. It is the killing at Badr, the famine of seven years, and the punishment of the grave.

But most of them do not know that. Then He commanded him to be patient until the punishment befalls them, so He said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 48:

﴿And be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾, by their being given respite, and by the hardship that befalls you in this matter.

﴿For indeed you are under Our eyes﴾, meaning: in such a way that We see you and guard you. He used the plural "eyes" (a'yun) because the pronoun is in the plural form. Do you not see His saying: ﴿And that you may be brought up under My eye﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39]?

﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise when you arise﴾, for the prayer, and this is what is said after the takbir: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You" (Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika); or wherever you stand up from; or from your sleep.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 49:

﴿And glorify Him for part of the night and at the setting of the stars.﴾

And when the stars turn their backs (adbara) at the end of the night, "wa-adbar" is read as "wa-idbar" (with a kasra on the alif), meaning: in the wake of the stars and their traces, when they set. The intended meaning is the command to say "Subhan Allah wa-bihamdihi" (Glory be to God and praise be to Him) at these times. It was also said: "al-tasbih" (glorification) means the prayer, when one rises from his sleep; "min al-layl" means the two night prayers (salat al-'ishaayn), and "idbar al-nujum" means the dawn prayer (salat al-fajr).
